It addresses the computational bottleneck of non-collocated rendering where the light and camera are not at the same position, requiring expensive light-ray marching for each shading point [S1].

The claim states that the method addresses the computational bottleneck of non-collocated rendering (where light and camera are not at the same position) by avoiding expensive light-ray marching for each shading point. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms this: it notes that naive non-collocated rendering is 'very expensive' because it requires 'connecting each shading point to the light source with additional light-dependent opacity accumulation.' It further explains that the proposed method 'perform[s] ray marching from the light's point of view and precompute[s] the accumulated opacity,' allowing the system to 'directly sample from the precomputed volume' during rendering, thereby avoiding the expensive per-point accumulation.
